# Intake brief: measure idle-aware local admission over ≥24h

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the before/after effect of the idle-aware local admission
override measured over a full 24 h window, so I know whether spending idle GPU
time actually reduced paid remote fallbacks without harming interactive traffic.

## Context

`LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J` implements the override: when the local backend has been
idle for `server.local_idle_admit_seconds` (default 60) and nothing is queued,
in flight, or loading, an economic `large_context_bypass` is served locally
instead of falling back to a remote provider. Selected by
`server.local_idle_admit_enabled` (default **false**).

Instrumentation shipped with that change:

- `routing_idle_admit provider=… model=… reason=economic_bypass_idle
  idle_seconds=… threshold_seconds=… estimated_tokens=… new_tokens=…
  cached_ratio=… cache_state=… session=…`
- `proxy-usage-analysis` reports `Local admitted while GPU idle (cold-cache
  override)` in the report and `local_idle_admit` in the JSON/CLI counters.
- `/llama/local/status` publishes `local_idle_seconds`,
  `local_last_activity_at`, `local_last_activity_source`.

The measurement needs the change deployed and running for ≥24 h, so it cannot
complete inside the implementing session.

## Baselines (window 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23)
| Metric | Baseline |
| --- | ---: |
| Local serve share | 2.6 % |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,284 |
| `local_dispatch_denied` | 2,641 (187 in one hour with local busy at 2.5 %) |
| Remote fallback events | 17,076 |
| Local busy share of slot-hours | ~54 % (decode 29.3 %, prefill adds ~14.3 h) |
| Local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` | p50 61.8 s, p90 269.8 s, max 817 s |
| Prefills sharing the GPU | 47.8 % (p50 85 s overlapped vs 23.4 s solitary) |

## Acceptance criteria

1. A ≥24 h post-deploy window is analysed with `proxy-usage-analysis` and reports,
   next to the baselines above: `local_idle_admit` count, local serve share,
   `large_context_bypass` count, remote fallback count.
2. Idle-admitted requests' `dispatch_first_byte_ms` percentiles and total prefill
   slot-seconds are reported and compared with non-idle local dispatches at the
   same context bucket (they are expected to be **slow** — that is the trade —
   so the comparison must state sample counts and bucket sizes).
3. `local_dispatch_denied` does not increase and no mid-stream timeouts
   (`ReadTimeout`, `empty_response`) are attributable to idle-admitted requests
   (per-request correlation via session id, 60 s window).
4. Interactive traffic is not harmed: p50/p90 `dispatch_first_byte_ms` for high-
   priority requests is unchanged within noise, or the report states the
   regression with the causal evidence (idle-admitted prompt overlapping).
5. Either the override is confirmed worth enabling by default, or a concrete
   follow-up records the tuning (threshold, prompt-size cap, priority gating)
   and why.

## Risks / notes

- An idle-admitted 120K prompt can hold a slot for minutes; the override already
  refuses while anything is queued or in flight, so a same-window overlap is a
  real finding, not a config error.
- The idle signal is process-local monotonic time; a proxy restart resets the
  clock to process start (truthful, but note it when reading the first minutes
  after a restart).
- Coordinate with `LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K` (restored-prefix warmness measurement)
  and `LP-0MVGCQ421005IXGC` (report prefill/busy metrics) to avoid duplicate
  report plumbing.


## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`
data.title: Measure idle-aware local admission impact over >=24h (before/after)

# Intake brief: run the idle-admission measurement window

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-aware local admission override enabled for one
full ≥24 h window and analysed with `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, so
LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD's AC1–AC5 can be resolved (enable by default, or record
the tuning) with measured numbers instead of a counterfactual estimate.

## Why this is a separate item

LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD landed the measurement tooling (commit `c99ac884`):
`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, the `priority=`/`estimated_tokens=` dispatch
fields, `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` and the config documentation.
What it cannot do is satisfy its own ACs, because the override is **off by
default** (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled: false`) and zero
`routing_idle_admit` events exist in any logged window. Enabling it changes live
routing, and the 24 h window cannot elapse inside a session — hence this item.

## Steps

1. Decide whether to enable the override for the window (live routing change:
   idle GPU time is spent on economic bypasses instead of paid remote calls,
   at the risk of a long first byte on an idle-admitted 120 K prompt).
2. Set `server.local_idle_admit_enabled: true` (keep
   `server.local_idle_admit_seconds: 60` for the first window), restart the
   proxy via `/skill:start-proxy --restart`, and record the restart timestamp.
3. Wait ≥ 24 h (the window cannot be shortened).
4. Run:
   `python3 scripts/idle_admit_impact.py --before-start '<baseline 24 h>' --before-end '<...>' --after-start '<restart>' --after-end '<+24 h>' --deployed-at '<restart>' --window-closed --json > /tmp/idle_admit_24h.json`
   plus `--markdown` for the report section.
5. Record the numbers + verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD, then apply the AC5
   recommendation: keep the flag on (`enable_by_default`), or open the tuning
   follow-up the tool proposes and set the flag accordingly.

## Notes

- The baseline of record is 2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23 (table in the
  parent item and in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`).
- The counterfactual estimate over 2026-10-21 19:00 → 2026-10-22 19:00 was 937
  of 1,235 economic bypasses (75.9 %) with ≥ 60 s of system-wide local idle —
  the expected size of the win, not a measurement.
- Batch with LP-0MVGGPSVM003W35K (restored-prefix warmness, also waiting on a
  24 h post-deploy window) to avoid two separate experimental windows.
- `proxy-usage-analysis` reports the same override from the other side; use its
  05:00 daily report as the AC1 artifact of record when convenient.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The override has run for ≥ 24 h with `local_idle_admit` events > 0, and the
   window start is recorded (post-restart).
2. `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py --window-closed` runs clean on the window and
   its JSON artifact is attached to LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.
3. The AC1–AC4 numbers are recorded on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the
   2026-10-19/20 baseline.
4. The AC5 outcome is decided and recorded: either `enable_by_default` (flag
   stays on) or the tuning follow-up (threshold / prompt-size cap / priority
   gating) is filed with the measured evidence.


## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# Load-normalise the AC3 denial check in the idle-admit measurement

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the AC3 `local_dispatch_denied` check normalised to
window load (per bypass/fallback event), so the measured `+9.3 %` per-hour
denial "increase" (window 2026-10-22 21:48 → 2026-10-23 21:48, ~2× busier than
the before window) is judged on a load-independent signal instead of a
confounded raw rate.

## Measured evidence (artifact `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`)

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `local_dispatch_denied` raw | 66.0 /h | 72.1 /h | **+9.3 %** (> 5 % band → fail) |
| `large_context_bypass` events | 1,790 | 3,702 | +107 % |
| Remote fallback events | 6,953 | 12,888 | +85 % |
| Denials per bypass+fallback event | 1,584/8,743 = 0.181 | 1,731/16,590 = 0.104 | −42 % |

The raw rate cannot distinguish "the override causes more denials" from "a 2×
heavier window produces proportionally more denials". The tool currently
implements only the raw per-hour rate (`scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`:
`denied_before_rate`/`denied_after_rate`, `_DENIED_TOLERANCE_PCT = 5.0`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` reports a load-normalised denial rate — denials per bypass+fallback event — alongside the existing per-hour rate, in both the AC3 check and the JSON/markdown output.
- The AC3 verdict uses the normalised rate for pass/fail (the raw per-hour rate remains reported), so a raw increase caused purely by higher load no longer fails the check; a genuine per-event increase still fails.
- Tests cover: the normalised-rate arithmetic against the exact window numbers above (fail → pass), a synthetic per-event denial increase that still fails the check, and backward compatibility of all existing JSON keys and exit codes.
- Re-running the tool `--window-closed` on the closed window records the AC3 verdict on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD next to the baselines table, with the normalised numbers and sample counts.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` documents the normalised metric definition and why the raw per-hour rate is load-confounded.

## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`

# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the post-flip window measured against the ≥24 h pre-flip
baseline and a keep/rollback verdict recorded, so the sweep is judged by its
own flip criteria instead of by assumption.

Part of LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R. Delivers the evaluation half of parent AC1
(trigger, observation window, verdict) and AC3's "run the report and record the
numbers".

## Nature of the task

This is a **scheduled measurement task, not code work**. It starts only after
the sweep child has shipped to `dev`, been released, and the proxy has been
restarted in a quiet window. It is expected to stay open for the 7-day
observation window; it must not be implemented inside a code session.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — sweep plan.** This item records the target values (30 s / depth 2),
   the trigger, window, flip criteria and rollback, verified against the
   deployed state before the flip is announced.
2. Preconditions verified and recorded on this item: the reservation endpoint
   is live, the ≥24 h pre-flip baseline exists (report/baseline child), the
   sweep is deployed (config 30 s / depth 2 active after a quiet-window
   restart), and the flip is announced in a comment with the restart
   timestamp.
3. `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` is run over the 7-day post-flip
   window (≥1 000 queue events), with numbers recorded: dead wait per hour vs
   baseline, residual wins as a share of queue events, remote dispatch volume
   change, ticket-backed dispatch count, and the lease-active vs `none` loss
   split.
4. A keep/rollback verdict is recorded against the three flip criteria —
   ≥50 % fall in dead wait per hour, residual wins ≥20 % of queue events,
   remote dispatch volume rise <20 % relative. A rollback reverts the two
   values to 60 / 8, restarts the proxy, and records the observed numbers.
5. If the window is incomplete (fewer than 1 000 queue events, a log-coverage
   gap, or no restart yet), the item stays `blocked`/`open` with the shortfall
   and the missing days stated — never a verdict from partial data.

## Key Files

- `scripts/contention_queue_sweep_report.py` (consumed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (rollback only)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the sweep child (30 s / depth 2 deployed) and the report/baseline
  child (baseline + tool).

## Goal

As an implementer of the GPU telemetry slices (parent LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W) I need
shared, deterministic verification assets — `/slots` payload fixtures, recorded
Prometheus HTTP API payloads, and a `gpu_busy_percent` guard that also covers the
new CLI — so every later child starts from a failing test instead of from code.

## Context

This is the **test-first slice** of the parent plan. It changes no production
behaviour: it delivers the verification harness that the sampler (sibling
"Publish slot occupancy metrics from the proxy"), the recording rule (sibling
"Combined computing-workload recording rule") and the CLI (sibling
"`gpu_utilisation` CLI with honest unknown share") consume.

Live evidence gathered while planning (2026-10-29, this host): the deployed
llama.cpp build answers `GET :8080/slots?model=mxbai-embed` with
`[{"id":0,"n_ctx":256,"speculative":false,"is_processing":false}, ...]` — no
`id_task` and no `next_token` while idle. Fixtures must therefore cover both this
build's shape and the older/richer shape that carries `id_task`/`next_token`.
`curl localhost:8000/slots` returns 404 (the proxy does not expose `/slots`), as
the parent brief states.

## Minimal implementation

- Add fixtures next to the tests that use them (`proxy/tests/`, pytest `conftest.py`
  or a small `gpu_fixtures.py` helper) — payload builders, not golden blobs, so a
  case is one keyword argument away.
- Record Prometheus API payloads as JSON under `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` with a
  small README line saying how each was captured (endpoint + query + window).
- Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES` scanning in
  `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` to include `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Reusable fixtures exist for a healthy `/slots` payload (mixed `is_processing`), an empty payload, a richer payload carrying `id_task`/`next_token`, and failed fetches (HTTP 500, timeout, connection error) — each fixture is asserted to have the shape its consumer expects.
- [ ] Recorded `query_range` payloads exist under `monitoring/tests/fixtures/` for `gpu:computing:bool`, `gpu:computing_workload:bool`, `gpu:power_watts:amdgpu`, `llama_slots_busy`, `llama_slots_sample_timestamp_seconds` and `up{job="llama-proxy"|"node-exporter"}`, including one stream with a deliberate gap of missing samples; each file documents the endpoint, query and window it was captured from.
- [ ] The `gpu_busy_percent` guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` also scans `scripts/gpu_utilisation.py` and fails if the series appears in any query expression, while still allowing documentation/comment mentions.
- [ ] A regression test asserts that the guard fails on a synthetic expression containing `gpu_busy_percent` and passes on the real files (the guard must not be vacuously green).
- [ ] Every test asserts observable behaviour (fixture shape, guard outcome, exact split), not merely that a value is non-`None`.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/conftest.py` / `proxy/tests/gpu_fixtures.py` (new or extended)
- `monitoring/tests/fixtures/slots_api_responses.json` (new)
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_gpu_telemetry_sampler.py` (fixture consumers land here later)

## Notes

Keep this slice small: only fixtures and guards that at least one sibling child
actually consumes. If a sibling ends up needing a different shape, extend the
fixture in that child rather than pre-building speculative variants.

# Goal

As the operator reading the 05:00 nightly report, I want the `slots_stale`
(stale-poll) rate rendered against its configurable target in `report.md` and
exposed in `--json`, so I can judge polling-path health without running
`scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` by hand and cross-checking two
surfaces.

Parent: **LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0** (delivers parent AC1; contributes to parent
AC3/AC4/AC5 and AC6). Decisions already taken in the parent Appendix — do not
re-litigate: **Q1 → (a)** edits under `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/**` are
authorised for the additive report surface only; **Q2 → (a)** the single shared
derivation lives in `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`; **Q3 → (a)** the target
is a new `--stale-rate-target` flag on `analyze_proxy_usage.py`, default 0.05.

This is the **first vertical slice** of the parent: parser → shared derivation →
aggregation → report section → JSON → CLI → tests → docs rows, all in one
deliverable increment (a tracer bullet ending in a rendered section, not a
horizontal layer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1.1 (single derivation).** The stale-rate derivation (status-poll
  detection, `slots_stale` / `slots_detail_stale` / `latency_ms` field
  extraction, the denominator that **excludes** polls with no `slots_stale`
  field, the rate, and the target check) exists once in
  `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`; `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  imports it instead of its private copies and its published figures for the
  2026-10-24 window are unchanged (11,654 status polls / 9,278 stale /
  79.61 %).
- **AC1.2 (parser).** `status_request` events carry additive `LogEvent` fields
  `slots_stale`, `slots_detail_stale` and `latency_ms` (`None` on pre-change
  lines); synthetic schema-1, schema-2 and schema-3 lines, stale and fresh,
  parse to the expected values and no other event kind is affected.
- **AC1.3 (half-open aggregation).** Status polls are aggregated with
  `[window_start, window_end)` semantics: a poll exactly at `window_start` is
  counted and one exactly at `window_end` is excluded, and the aggregation
  reports poll count, stale count, stale denominator and stale rate.
- **AC1.4 (stale rate section).** The nightly report renders a `slots_stale`
  section for its own window, inside `## Local capacity signals` (rendered
  immediately after `## Local contention prediction vs reality`), showing the
  status-poll count, the polls with `slots_stale=true`, the rate, the configured
  target and an explicit met/unmet outcome; the section is **omitted** (no
  zero-fill) when the window has no status polls.
- **AC1.5 (JSON).** `--json` gains an additive `capacity_signals.slots_stale`
  key (poll count, stale count, denominator, rate, target, passed) mirroring the
  section; every existing key keeps its current meaning.
- **AC1.6 (configurable target).** `analyze_proxy_usage.py` accepts
  `--stale-rate-target` (default `0.05`), threaded through `run_analysis` into
  both the rendered section and `--json`; a test asserts that an override
  changes the rendered target **and** the pass/fail outcome.
- **AC1.7 (tests).** New behaviour is covered by tests in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py` covering parser,
  aggregation (including the boundary case), rendering, JSON and a
  divergence test that fails when the nightly analyzer and
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` disagree on the same synthetic
  lines. The full project test suite passes (run through the test skill, never
  an ad-hoc pytest).
- **AC1.8 (unattended safety).** A window with no status polls, and a log
  directory with no logs at all, render a clean report and exit 0 without
  raising — the 05:00 cron must never fail on an empty window.

## Minimal implementation

- **New** `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py`: stdlib-only pure helpers
  (`is_status_poll`, `status_fields`, stale-rate/denominator derivation, target
  check). Must **not** import `.pi/**` (mirrors `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py`).
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`: drop the private copies, import the
  shared helpers natively, keep every published figure identical.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`: new regexes and
  additive `LogEvent` fields on the `status_request` branch.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`: half-open status-poll
  aggregation stored on `AnalysisResult` (e.g. `capacity_signals`).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`: `## Local capacity
  signals` skeleton with the `slots_stale` rows plus the `capacity_signals`
  JSON key; `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`:
  `--stale-rate-target` flag threaded to `run_analysis`.
- The skill reaches `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` through the documented
  path-based shim precedent already used by
  `tests/test_admission_rate_bucket_report.py` (the 05:00 cron runs from the
  repo root).

## Key Files

- `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` (new)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_capacity_signals.py` (new)

## Method

TDD within the slice: write the failing parser / aggregation / render / JSON /
boundary tests first, then the production change, then one commit that keeps the
suite green (the repo gate forbids committing a red tree, so the tests and the
code they exercise land in the same slice).

## Risks

- **Divergent copies** — extracting helpers can leave a stale copy on either
  surface; the divergence test (AC1.7) must exercise both surfaces on the same
  synthetic lines.
- **Window drift** — the analyzer aggregates inclusively today; the half-open
  filter must apply to status polls without changing any existing section's
  counts (assert an existing behaviour test stays green).
- **Skill import fragility** — the path shim must fail closed with a clear error
  if the repo root is not on the path, never silently fall back to a copy.

## Deliverables

Shared module + refactored reference tool, parser/aggregation/reporting/CLI
changes, new test module, and the `slots_stale` rows of `SKILL.md` /
`REFERENCE.md` (the consolidated docs pass is the sibling docs item).

## Out of scope (parent scope-creep guard)

Attribution of stale polls by cache source (`slots_detail_stale`) or latency
band, and abandonment-event attribution, stay out of scope for this item and its
parent. `latency_ms` is parsed so the shared derivation stays aligned with the
reference tool, but no latency-band breakdown is rendered nightly; if it is
wanted, it is a follow-on item, not a widening of this one.
data.title: slots_stale rate published end-to-end in nightly report

# Goal

Document the new capacity-signal surface so the next operator (or agent)
reading `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` can read
the section, override the stale-rate target, and understand exactly how the
live-work derivation pairs with `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
without reading the code.

Parent: **LP-0MVRMHY0F007RWA0** (delivers parent AC5). Depends on the two
implementation slices — document the surface **as built**, not as planned.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC5.1 (documentation).** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` and
  `REFERENCE.md` describe the `## Local capacity signals` section: which
  figures it carries (poll count, `slots_stale` count/rate, `capacity_hint`
  counts and shares, saturated-without-live-work count and shares), when it is
  omitted, and where it is rendered in `report.md`.
- **AC5.2 (JSON keys documented).** `REFERENCE.md` documents the additive
  `capacity_signals` keys (`slots_stale`, `capacity_hint`,
  `saturated_without_live_work`, `targets`) with their field meanings, and
  states that the pre-existing `status_capacity_hint` /
  `denial_attribution.capacity_hint` keys are unchanged.
- **AC5.3 (target documented).** The `--stale-rate-target` flag is documented
  with its `0.05` default, how an override flows into both the Markdown and the
  JSON, and how to set it on the 05:00 cron line — with a copy-pasteable
  example.
- **AC5.4 (derivation documented consistently).** The docs describe the
  schema-2/schema-3 live-work derivation and the stale-rate denominator
  (polls without a `slots_stale` field excluded, never counted as fresh) in
  wording consistent with the `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`
  docstring and the shared `scripts/lib/capacity_signals.py` module — no
  contradictory description of the same rule.
- **AC5.5 (caveats retained).** The docs keep the caveat that the stale rate is
  a *polling-path* signal, meaningful only for the build it was measured on,
  and note the retained-log coverage limitation.
- **AC5.6 (cron unchanged).** The docs state that the nightly pipeline gained no
  network call, LLM call or interactive prompt, and that an empty window
  renders cleanly.

## Minimal implementation

- Update `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` (usage + interpretation
  section) and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` (JSON reference
  section).
- Cross-link the two documents to
  `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` for the standalone equivalent.
- No code change; if the built behaviour differs from these ACs, fix the docs to
  match the built behaviour and note the deviation in the item (do not "fix" the
  code from a docs item).

## Key Files

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md`
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`

## Risks

- **Doc drift** — the shared derivation currently lives in two descriptions
  (skill docs, tool docstring); AC5.4 requires one consistent wording, with the
  module docstring as the source of truth.

## Deliverables

Updated `SKILL.md` and `REFERENCE.md` with section, keys, flag/override, cron
example, derivation rule and caveats.

## Goal

Produce the evidence trail that the new pushed-commit guard works on the real clone, not only
in the hermetic sandbox: a genuine refusal for a mismatched sha, and a green `dev` push whose
full-suite cache entry is keyed to the pushed commit (the parent's AC3).

## Context

- Parent LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9 AC3: "A green `dev` push from a clean checkout at the pushed
  commit still leaves a full-suite cache entry keyed to that commit (`run_tests.py --summary`
  reports it)".
- The observed defect (LP-0MVMC1AD0013HND, 2026-10-28): gate green in seconds,
  `run_tests.py --summary` reported `missing` for the pushed commit.
- The hermetic tests use a fake runner, so they cannot prove the cache entry really lands at
  the pushed commit; only a real push can.

## Deliverables

Redefine `remote-ok` to *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: it keeps the local route and never waits for a slot (parent AC15, AC16, AC20). This child lands **before** the default inversion so the suite stays green - today `remote-ok` is a non-default value, so changing its meaning breaks no headerless caller.

## Goal

Make the value that will become the default safe to be the default: it attempts local when a slot is free, and steps straight to the next provider in the chain when local cannot serve the request right now - no queue entry, no deferral, no local-capacity `429`.

## Scope

- `apply_local_preference()` loses `strip_by_preference`; the capacity strip (`CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`) and its remote-less carve-out are kept byte-identical, so no preference can empty a chain.
- Remove (or neutralise) both dead `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: ... "providers": []` branches in the two dispatch cycles.
- `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` declines to enqueue for `remote-ok`, returning the `"fallback_policy"`-equivalent outcome so the caller falls through immediately.
- Docstrings for `apply_local_preference`, `local_preference_for_request` and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` state the new meaning and the historic-name warning.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`: the preference-table row for `remote-ok` and the per-exit fall-through notes that describe the strip are re-anchored on the capacity strip alone (no preference-based strip exists any more).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/priority.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_only_exit_docs.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_capacity_signal_verification.py`

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (no preference strip: `remote-ok` keeps the local route, parent AC15).** `apply_local_preference()` (`priority.py:459-474`) no longer filters on `preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK`: the only preference-independent strip that remains is the capacity strip (`verdict == CAPACITY_TOO_LARGE`), with its existing remote-less carve-out. `remote-ok` therefore means *"local allowed, remote acceptable"*: the local entry stays in the chain and is attempted exactly as a headerless request attempts it today. A test row asserts a `remote-ok` request attempts local (the upstream calls include the local provider, `X-Local-Route: local`) when local can serve, and that `PREF_REMOTE_OK` produces no `providers`-stripping in `effective_chain_for_request()`.
- **AC3 (no preference can empty a chain, parent AC16).** The `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` is served locally (200, zero remote calls); the `private` model + absent header is unchanged at this stage; a normal chain with local down serves from the next remote entry, and exhaustion only when nothing is left to try. The two dead empty-chain branches are gone (grep-asserted). **Restates parent AC16:** Removing the preference strip makes the empty-chain hazard disappear rather than moving it: `apply_local_preference()` can only strip for capacity, and that strip already returns a remote-less chain intact (`priority.py:470-474`). Two branches that exist only to serve the old `remote-ok`-strips-everything behaviour must be removed or neutralised: the `elif _preference == PREF_REMOTE_OK: … providers: []` fallbacks in both dispatch cycles (`provider.py:11445`, `:12142` as of 2026-10-30). Test rows: (a) `private` model (single `type: local` provider, `config.yaml:400-408`) + absent header ⇒ 200 served **locally**, no exhaustion body, zero remote calls; (b) `private` model + explicit `remote-ok` ⇒ same; (c) `remote-ok` on a normal chain with local down ⇒ the next remote entry serves (exhaustion only when there is genuinely nothing left to try).
- **AC4 (immediate step, no queue, parent AC20).** For each local-exit cause enumerated in parent AC20 (slot saturated, prefill-ETA over budget, local cooldown, residency/thrash skip, lease held, per-entry context cap) a `remote-ok` request produces `X-Local-Route: remote`, a `contention_queue` wait of 0, and exactly one upstream call. `high` priority keeps its existing never-queue semantics.
- **AC5 (documentation matches, parent AC12 slice).** `routing.md` no longer states that `remote-ok` removes the local route, the historic-name warning is present, and the pinned exit-table docs test (`test_local_only_exit_docs.py`) passes with the re-anchored `too_large` rows.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the preference strip in `apply_local_preference()`; keep the capacity strip and carve-out untouched.
2. Delete the two `PREF_REMOTE_OK` empty-chain branches.
3. Add the `remote-ok` early decline in `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot()` (before the reservation/ticket handling so no ticket is consumed for a request that will not wait).
4. Update the three docstrings and the `routing.md` rows.
5. Fill in the `remote-ok` rows of the contract specs from the previous child.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child.

Retire the deprecated `local-only` wire value with a **loud** `400` (parent AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4): never a silent demotion to `local-preferred` and never a silent resolution to the default. This child also builds the retirement mechanism that the later `prefer-local` retirement reuses, so the two retirements share exactly one implementation.

## Goal

A client still sending `local-only` gets an attributable, actionable failure instead of a policy it did not ask for (silent demotion to a local-first default could bill a cost-capped client - the LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG lesson).

## Scope

- Remove the `local-only` entry from `LEGACY_PREFERENCE_ALIASES` (and delete the alias table if nothing remains in it) and drop `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` from the live vocabulary.
- Extend the **single** parse/validation site (`admission_reserve.parse_preference()`) with a retired-value outcome carrying the retired value and its successor guidance; no second parser and no per-call-site comparison.
- Emit the `400` at the request entry point **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written; the body is stable (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only *chain*).
- Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection, carrying the retired value, the successor guidance and the session id when present.
- Scope guard (parent AC3): provider names, the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` reason token stay unchanged.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_preference_vocabulary_v2.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (loud rejection, parent AC1).** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` returns `400` with `code: local_preference_retired` and the successor guidance, emitted before routing: the fake transport records zero upstream calls, and no queue entry, lease or cooldown state is created. **Restates parent AC1:** `X-Local-Preference: local-only` is no longer normalised to `local-preferred`. It is rejected with `400` and a stable JSON body (`error`, `code: local_preference_retired`, a `detail` naming `local-preferred` as the successor and pointing a zero-remote-spend client at a local-only chain rather than a preference value), emitted **before** any routing, queueing, lease, dispatch or cooldown state is written (fake transport records zero upstream calls). It must **not** silently degrade to the active default (`remote-ok`, AC21): a silent demotion would let a cost-capped client be billed without consent — the exact 2026-10-25 defect (LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG) — and would make the retirement unobservable.
- **AC2 (not silently demoted, parent AC1).** No code path maps `local-only` to `local-preferred` or to `DEFAULT_PREFERENCE`; a test asserts the response is a rejection even when the local route is free and the request would otherwise succeed locally.
- **AC3 (attributable, parent AC2).** Exactly one `WARNING` per rejection naming the retired value, the successor and the session id when one is present; a test asserts a single line and its fields.
- **AC4 (vocabulary, parent AC4).** The alias table no longer contains `local-only` (asserted so the removal cannot silently regress); `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` keep their exact pre-change parse results; an unknown value still falls back to the default. **Restates parent AC4:** `parse_preference({"x-local-preference": "local-only"})` returns the retired outcome (a `local_preference_retired` rejection, never `local-preferred` and never the default); `local-preferred` and `remote-ok` keep today's exact result; the absent header resolves to the new default `remote-ok` (AC21); one test asserts the alias table no longer contains `local-only` so the removal cannot silently regress.
- **AC5 (scope discipline, parent AC3).** Grep-asserted: the provider fixtures named `local-only`, the `local_only_refused` log prefix, the `_build_local_only_refusal*` builders and the `local_only_no_local_route` token are untouched. **Restates parent AC3:** Only `X-Local-Preference` vocabulary changes. Explicitly unchanged: a provider *named* `local-only` (test fixtures in `proxy/test_home_page.py`, the `private` model notes), the refusal log prefix `local_only_refused`, the internal builders (`_build_local_only_refusal_response`, `_build_local_only_refusal_for_remote`, `_log_local_only_refusal`), and the canonical reason token `local_only_no_local_route`. Rationale: renaming them is churn that breaks log-grep consumers for no behavioural gain — recorded as a scope decision, not an oversight.
- **AC6 (documented, parent AC12 slice).** `routing.md` and the `config.yaml` commentary describe the retirement and the exact `400` shape with a migration note; the "clients may keep sending `local-only`" paragraph is removed.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Delete the alias mapping and the live constant; keep `PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` only as a retired-value registry entry naming its successors.
2. Add the retired outcome to `parse_preference()` and thread it through the request entry point (fail closed before dispatch).
3. Add the rejection warning and the stable body at the same place the other preference `400`s are built.
4. Update docs/config commentary and fill in the corresponding contract specs.

Blocked by the contract-test child.

Bound `local-preferred` deferral at **three** consecutive retryable local-capacity refusals, then let the request fall back to remote instead of emitting a fourth `429` (parent AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10). Reuses the existing retryability decision and the existing promotion shape - no third promotion path and no second classification.

## Goal

An unattended `local-preferred` worker currently spins on retryable `429`s for as long as the GPU stays contended (the 2026-10-25 incident shape). After three refusals it must get an answer from a paid tier, visibly, rather than nothing.

## Scope

- New bounded, TTL'd, per-session counter store (`proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py`, or an equivalent small dedicated module) keyed by the sanitised `X-Session-ID`; no unbounded growth, entry cap + TTL.
- Increment where `_refusal_retry_timing()` already decides retryability; the counter never re-classifies a refusal.
- At the threshold, strip the local entry for that request using `_promote_too_large_local_request()`'s shape and stamp `X-Local-Route: remote` + the new canonical token `deferral_refusals_exhausted` (registered in `LOCAL_FALLBACK_REASON_TOKENS`).
- Additive refusal-body fields `deferral_refusals` and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third refusal), with every pre-existing field and header unchanged.
- Exactly one log line per escalation naming the session, the refusal count and the threshold.
- New config key `local_deferral_max_refusals` (default `3`, `0` disables) documented in `proxy/config.yaml` with the existing server-restart convention.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/local_deferral.py` (new module for the bounded counter store)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/tests/test_local_deferral_budget.py` (new, created by the contract-test child)

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (bounded budget, parent AC5).** Refusals 1, 2 and 3 are unchanged in timing and shape (`retryable: true`, `Retry-After`/`retry_at`, `X-Local-Route: refused`); the fourth request from the same session is **not** refused - the local entry is dropped for that request and the remote tier serves it.
- **AC2 (visible, never silent, parent AC6).** The escalation returns the upstream status with `X-Local-Route: remote` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason: deferral_refusals_exhausted`; exactly one log line names the session, count and threshold; the escalation is distinguishable from a `too_large` promotion in both header and log; no `Retry-After` is advertised on the terminal path.
- **AC3 (the refusal advertises its budget, parent AC7).** The body reports `deferral_refusals` (count so far) and `deferral_refusals_remaining` (0 on the third), purely additive - pre-existing fields, headers and key order unchanged.
- **AC4 (lifecycle and bounded memory, parent AC8).** The counter resets on a successful local dispatch, on a non-retryable refusal or `too_large` promotion, on TTL expiry, and on `local_deferral_max_refusals` reconfiguration; the store is capped and TTL'd; a request with no resolvable session id keeps today's unbounded behaviour. One test per reset trigger.
- **AC5 (one knob, parent AC10).** `local_deferral_max_refusals` is the only threshold source (default `3`); `0` restores unbounded deferral; documented as restart-required; no other default changes.
- **AC6 (no queue/lease leak, parent Constraints).** An escalated request never first enqueues and then dispatches remotely - the escalation decision is made before queue entry (or the entry is released), asserted with the fake transport.
- **AC7 (cost-capped escape hatch, parent AC9).** A remote-less chain (`private`) keeps refusing after the third refusal instead of escalating; the pin-local predicate and its five call sites agree on the escalation decision.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the counter store with TTL, cap and a reset API; unit-test it directly.
2. Hook the increment into the single retryability decision and the reset into the local-success / `too_large` / non-retryable paths.
3. Reuse the `too_large` promotion shape for the escalation and register the token in the single token table.
4. Add the two body fields in the single refusal builder and the escalation log line.
5. Add the config key and its commentary, then fill in the deferral-budget specs.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the contract-test child. Independent of the vocabulary children (do not rebase its counter onto a preference comparison - use the existing pin predicate).

# Record and re-verify abandoned slot identity on every release path

## Summary

Make every abandonment path either name the slot the backend is still draining
or record an explicit endpoint-wide "unknown slot" entry, so nothing the proxy
gave up on is ever unattributable.

Parent: LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — AC1, AC2, and the annotation half of AC3.

## Target outcome

A draining slot the proxy abandoned is *always* matchable from the registry:
the 7 attributable-but-unannotated polls (shape 1) and the 5 unattributable
`measured_cache_deficit` polls (shape 2) both gain a registry entry.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Every abandonment path records a registry entry that can match the slot it** gave up on, or an endpoint-wide entry the status builder can match.
- **AC2 — A drained-but-still-`is_processing` slot is annotated `abandoned_busy`** until llama-server reports it free, TTL-bounded, no leak.
- `_record_abandoned_slot` no longer silently drops an abandonment: an
  unresolvable slot identity records an endpoint-wide entry (a documented
  sentinel key that cannot collide with an `int` slot id) carrying
  `slot_id=None`, `endpoint`, `session_id`, `reason`, `abandoned_at`,
  `ttl_seconds` and a `scope` field (`"slot"` | `"endpoint"`).
- Every recording path reaches that behaviour: prefill deadline, client
  disconnect, no-progress watchdog, orphan sweep, session eviction and the
  measured-cache-deficit abort (`_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`, which
  currently passes neither slot id nor stream). A test asserts an entry exists
  for each path when the slot is unresolvable.
- `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch` forwards the dispatch record's
  pinned slot identity (and its `stream_cm`) instead of relying on a
  post-free session lookup, so the upstream cancel and the annotation both
  fire on the earliest-abort path.
- The resolved id is re-verified against the slot the backend actually reports
  (session/record binding captured *before* the assignment is freed). On
  mismatch the release logs `abandoned_slot_mismatch` with
  `recorded_slot=`, `observed_slot=` and still records the endpoint-wide
  entry, so shape 1 becomes diagnosable rather than silent.
- Log lines carry `slot_source=explicit|assignment|endpoint_wide` so the
  intake OPEN QUESTION ("why did the 7 attributable polls show
  `local_abandoned_slots=0`") is answerable from production logs.
- Registry invariants hold: in-process, keyed `(endpoint, key)`, lazily
  pruned, TTL-bounded (`DEFAULT_ABANDONED_SLOT_TTL_SECONDS`, 900 s), no timer
  task, re-abandoning refreshes, entry count bounded by `(endpoint, slot)`
  pairs plus one endpoint-wide entry per endpoint.
- The annotation path still never frees/acquires capacity, decrements counters
  or creates a lease (assert in tests).

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: add the endpoint-wide sentinel and a
  `scope` field in `_record_abandoned_slot`; record instead of returning
  `None`; extend `_abandoned_slot_lookup`/`_release_unserved_dispatch` to
  capture the record's pinned slot before the free and to log
  `slot_source`; keep `_abandoned_slot_for` exact-match precedence.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`: pass the record slot + `stream_cm` from
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`.
- `proxy/proxy/server.py`: session-eviction slot capture already resolves per
  record — route it through the same "record or endpoint-wide" helper so an
  unresolvable record still annotates.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **Deterministic tests: endpoint-wide abandonment annotation**
  (test first, then this item makes them pass).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — registry, `_record_abandoned_slot`,
  `_abandoned_slot_for`, `_release_unserved_dispatch`,
  `_release_measured_cache_abort_dispatch`
- `proxy/proxy/server.py` — `session_evicted` slot resolution
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline/measured-cache abort call sites
- `proxy/tests/test_abandoned_local_dispatch.py` — path coverage

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the `local_lease_active` re-queue path to
honour the request's priority and to charge a request's queue budget **once per
turn**, so a `high`-priority request is never parked there and a request that
already waited cannot be handed a fresh 60 s.

## Defects found by code reading (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

`proxy/proxy/provider.py` has two `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites:

1. the `local_concurrency_limit` check — passes `priority=_priority`;
2. the `local_lease_active` retry (entered after the local dispatch returned a
   `local_lease_active` 503) — passes **no `priority=`**, so `priority=None`
   reaches both `_contention_queue_enabled(config, priority)` and
   `_prefill_admission_guard(..., priority=priority)`. The documented contract
   is that `high` priority **never queues**; on this path that contract is not
   enforced, and the guard pricing no longer knows the priority either.

Second defect: the lease-active path re-enters the queue **after** the request
already spent its wait (or none) at the concurrency gate, and nothing carries
the spend forward — `_contention_queue_remaining_seconds` is computed for the
*response* but the *next* `wait_for_local_slot` is called with the full
`max_wait_seconds`. A request can therefore accumulate up to two full budgets
in one turn, which inflates both the abandoned-wait denominator and the user's
latency (measured: 368 lease-active waits vs 143 dispatches in the post-change
24 h window, 61.1 % abandoned).

## Scope (bug fix, test-first)

- Pass the priority through on the lease-active call site.
- Carry the spent queue wait on the request and bound the second wait by the
  measured remainder, so cumulative queue wait never exceeds
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` for one turn.
- Keep the guardrails: no new knob, no change to the 60 s / 120 s values.

## Minimal implementation

- `provider.py`: `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot(..., priority=_priority)` at the
  lease-active site; read/write the spent-wait marker through the existing
  `_set_queue_wait_on_request` / request attribute used by the deferral path,
  and pass `max_wait_seconds = min(cq_max, remainder)` (a keyword or a new
  helper argument on `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot`, defaulting to today's
  behaviour for callers that pass nothing).
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`: optionally accept an already-spent
  duration so the waiter's own bookkeeping/`queued_duration` reflects the
  cumulative wait (no change to wake-up logic).
- Tests first: high-priority lease-active request does not queue
  (`fallback_policy`-equivalent, no `contention_queue_wait`); a request with a
  spent wait gets at most the remainder; an untouched path behaves
  byte-for-byte as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `local_lease_active` retry call site passes the request's priority, and a unit test asserts a `high`-priority request never waits in that queue (returns without a queue wait, matching the documented `high` never-queues contract).
- AC2: A request that already spent queue wait in the same turn is bounded by the measured remainder at the second wait, and a unit test asserts cumulative queue wait ≤ `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (no second full budget).
- AC3: `queued_duration` / the logged wait for the lease-active path reflects the cumulative wait for the turn (observable), and the `trigger=`/`cause=` fields from the observability sibling are populated on this path.
- AC4: Guardrails unchanged and asserted: `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60), `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120), ordering test `60 < 120 < 840 < 900` green; no new configuration knob.
- AC5: Full test suite green at the pushed commit; existing queue, deferral, reservation and lease tests pass unchanged in intent (any intent-preserving update is called out in the commit message).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (both `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` call sites)
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py` (or the closest existing lease/queue suites)

## Related

- Parent: `LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR`; blocked-by: trigger/cause observability.

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want the prefill-ETA admission guard (or the queue
admit criterion) to price the blocker class the diagnosis proves is holding the
slot — so a queue wait that cannot be served inside the 60 s budget is refused
up-front instead of burning the full budget and detouring remote — or, if the
diagnosis does not support a change, a committed decision that says so.

This is the behaviour-change slice. It is deliberately gated on the diagnosis
record so the change is driven by evidence, not by the assumption that the
guard is "too permissive".

## Context (parent LP-0MVV1V213002QAIR)

Measured in the post-change 24 h window: 314/517 enqueued waits abandoned, all
at the full budget; 225/314 were `reason=local_lease_active`; for the 176
abandonments with a session-level preceding guard decision, 170 were `admit`
with median `projected_wait_s = 35.8 s`. The guard's occupancy term prices peer
*prefill* service (including the re-priced occupant remaining new tokens from
`LP-0MVS9YK9P006M1NQ`) but not the *generation* time of a lease holder that
keeps the slot after its prefill.

## Scope

- Extend the projected-wait quantity so the diagnosed blocker class is priced
  (for example, a lease/decode hold term raised into the existing occupancy
  maximum — evidence can only raise the floor, never lower it), and/or refuse
  a queue admit whose remaining budget cannot outlast the blocker.
- Preserve every documented invariant: measured evidence can only raise the
  symmetric `eta * busy_slots` floor; fail-open on missing/invalid records;
  warm prompts unchanged; no new configuration knob; `high` priority never
  queues.
- Out of scope: capping the lease holder's consecutive renewals — that is
  `LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0`.

## Minimal implementation

- Test first: simulated blockers in `proxy/tests/` — (a) a blocker whose
  remaining generation/lease hold exceeds the remaining budget ⇒ refuse (or
  defer under the pin semantics), (b) a short-prefill blocker ⇒ admit exactly
  as today, (c) missing/invalid occupant record ⇒ fail-open (today's floor).
- Then the minimal guard change in `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (plus the
  caller plumbing in `provider.py`/`router_helpers.py` if the blocker snapshot
  is not already available) and the log fields that make the new term
  attributable.
- Document the rollback using existing knobs only
  (`local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`,
  `local_prefill_deadline_seconds: 0`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_occupancy_deadline_admission.py`, `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py`, `proxy/tests/test_occupant_remaining_rebase.py`

# Chat-model child-port fallback fires for unloaded local models (gpt120) — polls the router and pollutes the fallback signal

**Priority:** medium · **Type:** bug · **Scope decisions (producer, 2026-10-31):** **Q1 = A** (guard every proxy-initiated `/slots` poll through the shared path) · **Q2 = B** (router `/models` loaded set behind a short-TTL cached snapshot) · **Q3 = B** (block on LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW + LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL, then reuse both)

## Problem statement

When a chat request names a local model that is **not currently loaded** (e.g.
`gpt120` while `Qwen3` is resident), the proxy's slot-availability check still
tries to discover that model's child port, fails, and falls back to the router
— which then answers `GET /slots?model=gpt120` with HTTP 400. The fallback is
recorded as a genuine discovery regression (counter +
`slots_child_port_unavailable` warning), so an unloaded-model poll is
indistinguishable from the real regression signal the parent fix
(LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3) was built to expose.

## Evidence (measured)

- **Direct cause, reproduced from the production log**
  (`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log.2026-10-28_10.gz`, lines 8204–8205):

  ```text
  2026-10-28 10:45:00,400 - INFO - [local] POST .../v1/chat/completions
    body={"model":"gpt120", ... "reply OK" ...} session_id=b87b8e0c-...
  2026-10-28 10:45:00,404 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model
    child port discovered for model=gpt120; falling back to router port 8080 ...
  ```

  The warning fires **4 ms after** the chat request and `current_model=Qwen3`
  is reported by `/status` two seconds later — i.e. the caller is the chat
  dispatch path, not a status poll.
- **Call path:** `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`_check_slot_availability` call) →
  `router_helpers._check_slot_availability()` →
  `_resolve_local_slots_target(srv, model="gpt120", ...)` →
  `_discover_local_child_port()` finds no signal for `gpt120` →
  `_warn_child_port_fallback()` increments
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and emits the throttled WARNING, then the poll goes to the **router**.
- **Scale (from LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window evidence):** 2,407 router-responder
  `/slots` 400 responses across the 48 h superset (243 on 2026-10-27, 2,164 on
  2026-10-28, vs 86 on 2026-10-26). The 400 side is owned by
  LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8; this item owns the *fallback-signal* side and the
  needless request.
- **Counter readings:** unreadable for the window (serving pid replaced
  2026-10-30T10:35:07Z); post-window pid 3224511 read `2` in its first
  ~8.7 h. The live pid 3944027 emitted one warning at
  `2026-10-31T00:42:00.198Z` for `model=mxbai-embed` — a **loaded** model with
  no discoverable child port, i.e. exactly the shape AC2 must keep counting.
- **Behavioural equivalence of skipping:** in `_check_slot_availability()` only
  a `200` with zero free slots produces a 503; every non-200 (including the
  router's definitive 400) already falls through to `return None`. Skipping the
  poll for a definitively unloaded model therefore **does not change the
  admission decision** — it only removes the request, the counter increment and
  the warning.

## Users and impact

- **Operator / observability consumer** — user story: *As the operator, I want
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` and the
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning to fire only when a **loaded** model's
  child port cannot be discovered, so that a real child-port discovery
  regression cannot hide behind unloaded-model noise.*
- **herdr dispatcher / capacity signal (`/llama/local/status`)** — user story:
  *As the dispatcher, I want proxy `/slots` polling to stay off the router for
  models that are not loaded, so polls do not queue behind the busy child or
  add 4xx noise to the router access log.*
- **Router access-log reader** — user story: *As an operator triaging
  `llama-server.log`, I want the router-responder `/slots` 400 population to be
  attributable to genuine external probes, not to the proxy polling for models
  that are not loaded.*

## Existing state

- All proxy-initiated `/slots` queries route through
  `_resolve_local_slots_target()` (`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`), which
  rewrites the local router endpoint to the discovered child port and, on
  discovery failure, calls `_warn_child_port_fallback()` (counter + throttled
  warning; LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC2/AC3).
- `_discover_local_child_port()` correctly returns `None` for a model with no
  child instance — the defect is that "no child instance because the model is
  not loaded" is treated as a *discovery failure* rather than a definitive
  non-stale answer.
- An authoritative "is this model loaded" primitive already exists:
  `srv.router_is_model_loaded()` / `srv.router_list_models()`
  (`proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py:997–1075`), reading the router's `/models`
  (`status.value` = loaded/ready/running/active), with presence-with-no-status
  treated as loaded.
- `srv.current_model` is set to the loaded llama model name in router mode
  (`lifecycle.py:2383`) **but** at startup it is first set to
  `router_preload_list[0]` (`server.py:949`), which can be a non-chat preset
  (`mxbai-embed`) — see the live warning above.
- The `/health` reachability probe no longer queries `/slots`
  (LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0), which is why the residual fallback signal is now
  dominated by this chat-path case.

## Desired change (scope settled — see Appendix)

1. **Guard before polling.** Before issuing `GET /slots?model=<m>` against the
   local router, establish whether `<m>` is loaded. When it is **definitively
   not loaded**, skip the poll entirely: no router request, no
   `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` increment, no
   `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning. There is no slot state to learn for
   a model with no instance. **Q1 = A:** the guard lives in the single shared
   `/slots` resolution path, so *every* proxy-initiated poll inherits it —
   chat-dispatch availability check, per-model poller, and the status/SSE
   paths.
2. **Keep the genuine signal.** A `/slots` poll for a **loaded** model whose
   child port cannot be discovered must still increment the counter and emit
   the throttled warning (AC2).
3. **Source of truth for "loaded" (Q2 = B).** Use the router's `/models`
   loaded set (existing `router_is_model_loaded()` / `router_list_models()`)
   behind a short-TTL cached snapshot; when the probe fails or the name cannot
   be resolved, **poll as today — never skip**. A false skip would remove a
   legitimate availability gate.
4. **Reuse, don't duplicate (Q3 = B).** The cached `/models` id snapshot is
   delivered by **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** and the `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
   section AC4 edits here overlap **LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL**; this item is blocked
   on both and reuses their artefacts.
5. **Observability of the skip (AC6, agent-proposed).** A dedicated counter
   (e.g. `llama_slots_child_port_skipped_total{reason="model_not_loaded"}`) or
   an equivalent documented signal so a skip is distinguishable from "never
   polled" when verifying AC1 on a live proxy.
6. **Docs.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` (observability / target-signal
   sections) and the resolver docstring plus the `proxy/README.md`
   child-port-discovery section must describe the unloaded-model skip and its
   signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Unloaded model is not counted.** A `/slots` poll for a model that
      is not currently loaded does **not** increment
      `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
      and emits no `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning (asserted via the
      counter/warning in a test; the router is not contacted).
- [ ] **AC2 — Loaded-model regression still pinned.** A `/slots` poll for the
      loaded chat model whose child port cannot be discovered **still**
      increments the counter and emits the throttled warning (regression test,
      must fail if the guard swallows loaded-model discovery failures).
- [ ] **AC3 — `/status` capacity truth preserved.** `/status` continues to
      report truthful capacity (existing "definitive model absent" behaviour:
      fail-open on the configured pool, no resurrected fossil counts).
- [ ] **AC4 — Documentation.** `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` observability
      section and the `_resolve_local_slots_target()` /
      `_discover_local_child_port()` docstrings in
      `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` describe the unloaded-model skip; the
      `proxy/README.md` child-port-discovery section agrees.
- [ ] **AC5 — Full suite green.** Full project test suite passes with the
      change (run through the test skill; changed-scope gate first).
- [ ] **AC6 — Skip is observable (agent-proposed; no producer objection).**
      Live/`/metrics` evidence distinguishes a skipped poll from a poll that
      was never attempted (new counter or documented log line), so AC1 can be
      verified post-deploy.
- [ ] **AC7 — Admission outcome unchanged.** A test pins that skipping the
      availability check for an unloaded model returns the same admission
      result (`None`) as the current definitive-400 fall-through — the fix must
      not start refusing or blocking requests.

## Constraints

- **No new router `/slots` traffic** and no new blocking call on the chat hot
  path: the "is it loaded" probe is `/models` only (never `/slots`), behind the
  short-TTL cached snapshot supplied by LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW.
- **Fail open, never fail closed:** when loadedness cannot be determined, poll
  as today. A wrong skip would remove a real availability gate and allow
  over-subscription of the slot pool.
- The guard is shared (Q1 = A): `_resolve_local_slots_target()` is
  **synchronous** while `router_is_model_loaded()` is **async** — the cached
  loaded snapshot must therefore be readable synchronously (refreshed by the
  async callers / a background refresh), or the resolver takes the loaded set
  as an argument supplied by its call sites.
- `_discover_local_child_port()` semantics stay unchanged (a missing signal is
  still "no port"); the definitive "model not loaded" classification is layered
  above it.
- Do not weaken the LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF AC3 guarantee for the loaded model.
- Do not build a second `/models` cache: reuse LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW's snapshot
  (Q3 = B); if that slice's API turns out to be unusable for a synchronous
  guard, raise it as a blocker rather than forking the cache.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — add the unloaded-model guard at the async
  `_check_slot_availability()` call site (and `_resolve_local_slots_target()`
  docs/metric plumbing); keep `_warn_child_port_fallback()` for loaded models.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — reuse `router_is_model_loaded()` /
  `router_list_models()`; add a short-TTL loaded-set cache (router pid keyed)
  if the guard needs one.
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — `poll_slots_for_model()` (the per-model poller
  resolves through the same path and must obey the same skip rule).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — fallback counter (unchanged) plus, if AC6 is
  accepted, the `skipped` counter.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_query_target_call_sites.py` — extend the shared
  resolver/call-site suite.
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_unloaded_model_skip.py` — new focused tests for
  AC1/AC2/AC7 (unloaded skip, loaded-model regression pinned, admission
  outcome unchanged).
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_availability_dedicated_client.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_child_port_discovery_rotation.py` — verify the guard did
  not disturb existing availability/discovery contracts.
- `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` — observability + "target signal going
  forward" sections.
- `proxy/README.md` — "Child-port discovery" / fallback-observability section.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — *Residual router-proxied `/slots` 500s: audit
  remaining call sites and enforce direct child-port polling* (done). Parent of
  the shared resolver, counter and throttled warning this item refines.
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — *Router `/slots` HTTP 400s: `?model=` resolution
  path* (plan_complete). Owns the 400-response side; its intake answer Q2=A
  established that a `?model=<unloaded>` 400 is *expected truth* — this item
  removes the proxy's **own** such polls without changing that stance. Its
  six slices (all `intake_complete`, blocked) overlap in two concrete places:
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** — *Resolve the model id from `/models` instead of
    hard-coding Qwen3* (slice 4). Delivers a **TTL-cached `/models` id
    snapshot** that the unloaded-model guard should reuse rather than
    duplicate (see Appendix Q2/Q3).
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZ7M002D9GT** — *Thread the resolved model through the
    model-less `/slots` probes* (slice 3). Its "skip the query when no model is
    known" is a **different** condition (empty model name) from this item's
    "model known but not loaded" — no AC overlap, but the same call sites.
  - **LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL** — *Document the model-resolution rule and 400
    semantics* (slice 5) touches the same `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md`
    section AC4 edits here — sequence or coordinate to avoid a doc conflict.
- **LP-0MVU7ZYLR0044D12** — *Static audit: enumerate every `/slots` 400 call
  path* (child of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8, intake_complete). Shares the call-site
  inventory this item needs.
- **LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0** — *Proxy `/health` reachability probe polls router
  `GET /slots?model=`* (completed). Removed the previously dominant
  fallback/500 source; that is why the chat-path case is now the visible one.
- **LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57** — *Verify `router:500 == 0` over 24 h after the
  child-port discovery fix*. Supplies the window evidence quoted above.
- **LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM** — *False "saturated" capacity signal starves herdr
  downtime dispatcher* (completed). Source of the definitive-model-absent /
  fail-open contract that AC3 and AC7 must preserve.
- **LP-0MTP1FQXH004JYEF** — model-filtered child-port discovery (`mxbai-embed`
  vs `Qwen3`), i.e. the reason a model name is passed to discovery at all.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (high impact): false "not loaded" ⇒ a real availability gate is
  skipped** and the pool can be over-subscribed. *Mitigation:* require an
  explicit `not loaded` answer from the router's `/models`; fail open to
  polling on any probe error or unresolved name; AC2 + AC7 tests pin both
  directions.
- **Risk: extra `/models` call per chat dispatch.** *Mitigation:* the shared
  short-TTL cached snapshot (LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW) — no new round trip on the
  hot path beyond one cache lookup.
- **Risk: name aliasing** (client model id ≠ llama model name ≠ router preset
  id). *Mitigation:* compare the already-resolved llama model name
  (`_resolve_slot_model_name`) case-insensitively; treat "unknown/not present"
  as *not* evidence of unloaded and poll as today.
- **Risk: `srv.current_model` is not a reliable loaded-set** (startup pins it
  to `router_preload_list[0]`, live example `mxbai-embed`; router mode can hold
  several loaded models). *Mitigation:* `/models` is the authority; treat
  `current_model` as a fallback only, and never as proof of absence.
- **Assumption:** the admission outcome for an unloaded model is unchanged
  because the current definitive-400 path already returns `None`
  (`_check_slot_availability` only 503s on `200` with zero free slots).
- **Assumption (Q3 = B):** LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW exposes the cached `/models` id
  snapshot in a form the synchronous resolver can read (directly or via an
  argument supplied by call sites). If it does not, that is a blocker to raise
  on this item rather than a reason to fork the cache.
- **Assumption:** "not loaded" polls carry no information for capacity
  signalling, so deleting them cannot degrade `/status` (which polls
  `srv.current_model`, i.e. a model it believes is loaded).
- **Scope-creep risk:** the startup `current_model = router_preload_list[0]`
  behaviour (and the resulting `mxbai-embed` warning) is a *separate* defect
  about loaded-model bookkeeping. Record as a linked follow-up rather than
  widening this item (see Appendix Q3).

## Dependencies / sequencing (Q3 = B)

- **Blocked by LP-0MVU7ZZIA0092AXW** — *Resolve the model id from `/models`
  instead of hard-coding Qwen3* (slice 4 of LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8). Supplies the
  TTL-cached `/models` id snapshot AC1/AC2/AC6 rely on.
- **Blocked by LP-0MVU7ZZTH005FSFL** — *Document the model-resolution rule and
  400 semantics* (slice 5). Owns the `docs/dev/slots-500-triage.md` section
  AC4 extends, so this item must not race it.
- Sequencing note: both blockers sit in the LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8 chain
  (`intake_complete`, serially blocked), so this item starts once slices 4 and
  5 are terminal. If slice 4 lands without a synchronously-readable snapshot,
  surface it as a blocker on this item rather than building a second cache.

## Out of scope

- Eliminating router `/slots` 400 responses in general (LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8)
  and the new per-query instrumentation deferred to LP-0MVTDMXXH005D5D5.
- `/health` reachability probing (already fixed in LP-0MVVCXUDZ007XID0).
- Changing `_discover_local_child_port()`'s discovery sources or caching.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded 2026-10-31 during the intake session for
LP-0MVVCY3HQ0009F0K (agent: Map; session
`herdr-1793416675-4166126-26041`). All three were raised as OPEN QUESTIONs
because the item was filed with "scope to confirm at intake", and all three
were answered by the producer on 2026-10-31 (interactive reply).
**Final: Q1 = A, Q2 = B, Q3 = B.**

- **Q1 — How wide is the skip?**
  - **A)** Guard **every** proxy-initiated `/slots` poll through the single
    shared path, so no proxy surface can poll a definitively unloaded model
    (chat-dispatch availability check, per-model poller, status/SSE paths —
